text:
deploy-bot: AUTOMATED ROLLBACK TRIGGERED for prod-canary at 1770022330
deploy-bot: reason=canary-5xx-spike error_rate=8.2% threshold=5%
deploy-bot: attempted rollback target=v2.3.6 status=STARTED

alex: saw the alert. did automated rollback start across all canaries?
maria: only canary-us-east shows the spike in traces, others look fine. attaching logs:
```
[2026-03-15T12:05:11Z] upstream_timeout service=runtime-infer host=gpu-23 502
[2026-03-15T12:05:14Z] kv-cache-miss model=redwood-3b seq=1024 latency=220ms
[2026-03-15T12:05:18Z] 504 grpc DEADLINE_EXCEEDED
```

ops_sre: rollback didn't finish, got blocked by a pin on dedicated pool for prod-canary. console shows pinnedVersion=v2.3.7 on DedicatedPool-08
jen: pinned? I thought the pin was only for dedicated prod-serving, not canary. how did canary end up there?
chris: quick context: we route a subset of canary traffic to dedicated for perf comparison. someone pinned v2.3.7 last week for a customer demo and forgot to unpin. rollback is trying to deploy v2.3.6 but the pool is pinned -> blocked.

alex: ok. options: 1) force-unpin then let automated rollback continue, 2) manually roll rest of canaries to v2.3.6 leaving dedicated pinned, 3) abort rollback and investigate. need decision now.
maria: customer impact? errors only on canary-us-east so far; no broad user-facing incidents. logs show model timeouts for long sequences.
jen: prefer to force-unpin then let rollback proceed, but confirm if that affects the demo customer (they were using dedicated pool).
chris: can confirm demo uses DedicatedPool-08, but their session is idle currently. unpin steps (CLI):
```
redwood dedicated-pool update --pool DedicatedPool-08 --unpin
redwood deploy rollback --env prod --target-version v2.3.6 --scope canary
```
ops_sre: running unpin now (will take ~30s).
ops_sre: unpin DONE. verified pool label pinnedVersion removed.
deploy-bot: MONITOR: rollback resumed for prod-canary status=IN_PROGRESS

maria: tailing canary logs... error_rate dropping to 1.1% on canary-us-east.
alex: good. can we confirm model caches were warmed? any KV cache invalidations to worry about?
chris: triggered a cache-warm job on the new version. command: `redwood cache prewarm --model redwood-3b --targets canary-us-east`
jen: communicating to sales/support: "no customer impact observed; automated rollback executed to v2.3.6 after canary spike; dedicated pool pin cleared". send to #customer-success?
sam_rm: put a short note in release notes under 2026-03-15: "v2.3.7 canary rollback due to canary 5xx spike; root cause: timing out model op on long sequences; pinned dedicated pool prevented auto-rollback until unpinned."

alex: action items: 1) ops to follow up on why demo pin not surfaced in release checklist (ops_sre) 2) infra to add alert when pool pinned (chris) 3) eng to run regression on long-seq latency (maria) 4) postmortem + customer comms (sam_rm)
ops_sre: noted. creating incident-XXXX and assigning.
chris: adding a pre-deploy check: `redwood dedicated-pool status --all | grep pinned` in the deploy CI step.
maria: will run extra evals against seq>2048 on canary today.
jen: thanks everyone. closing thread once postmortem doc is up. :white_check_mark:
